_about.model: Gaged Engineering GX9 CVT - 2-D longitudinal vehicle performance model
_about.units: SI throughout (m, kg, s, N, N*m, rad, rad/s). RPM only where noted.

provenance_legend.published: taken from a public Gaged Engineering / Briggs & Stratton / Baja SAE source
provenance_legend.derived: computed from published values by closed-form geometry (see gx9_params.m)
provenance_legend.nominal: REPRESENTATIVE ESTIMATE - measure your own hardware and replace before trusting results

engine._provenance: published: 10.0 hp class, ~14.7 ft-lb peak, Baja SAE spec Briggs & Stratton Model 19. Curve shape is nominal - replace with your dyno sheet.
engine.name: Briggs & Stratton Model 19 (Baja SAE spec)
engine._inertia_note: crank + flywheel + CVT primary, referred to the crankshaft

cvt._provenance: published: 3.9:1 low / 0.9:1 high ratio range, 6x6x5.75 in drive unit, 8x7x4.75 in driven unit. Radii/centre distance are derived to reproduce that range inside that envelope; spring, flyweight and helix values are nominal.
cvt.name: Gaged Engineering GX9
cvt._ramp_note: Combined ramp mechanical advantage x flyweight CG-radius growth. Tune this curve, not the flyweight mass, to move the shift point.
cvt._primary_preload_note: Sets engagement RPM: engagement occurs when m_w*w^2*R*phi(0) exceeds this preload (~2000 rpm with the nominal set).
cvt._torque_sense_lag_note: Belt/sheave compliance lag between transmitted torque and the helix reacting to it. Physically small; it also breaks the helix-force <-> belt-capacity algebraic loop so the model needs no loop solver.
cvt._shift_damping_note: Backshift is deliberately faster than upshift, as on real rubber-belt CVTs.

driveline._secondary_inertia_note: CVT secondary + gearbox, referred to the secondary shaft

vehicle._cg_note: cg_to_front_axle/wheelbase = static rear weight fraction (0.579 nominal). Drive is to the REAR axle.

scenario._accel_distance_note: 45.72 m = 150 ft, the Baja SAE acceleration event length.
